question: Effective resistance of the parallel combination of two resistors with 2 Ω and 3 Ω resistance, respectively, is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.2 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Formula for parallel resistance:** 1/R_effective = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/Rn, where R1, R2,... Rn are the resistances in parallel.
 
• **In this case:** R1 = 2 Ω and R2 = 3 Ω
 
• **Applying the formula:** 1/R_effective = 1/2 + 1/3
 
• **Finding a common denominator:** 1/R_effective = (3 + 2)/6
 
• **Simplifying:** 1/R_effective = 5/6
 
• **Solving for R_effective:** R_effective = 6/5 = 1.2 Ω
